ipc-title-link-no-icon ipc-title--on-textPrimary sc-7c95f518-2 ghWujX" data-testid="nlib-title"><a href="/name/nm0000031/?ref_=ls_t_6" class="ipc-title-link-wrapper" tabindex="0"><h3 class="ipc-title__text">6. Katharine Hepburn</h3></a></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-6 iDkHPP"><ul class="ipc-inline-list ipc-inline-list--show-dividers sc-7c95f518-4 lolxqE base" role="presentation" data-testid="nlib-professions"><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Actress</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Writer</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Soundtrack</li></ul><a class="ipc-link ipc-link--base sc-ab9eb9db-0 iRQWod" tabindex="0" aria-disabled="false" data-testid="nlib-known-for-title" href="/title/tt0032904/?ref_=ls_knf_6">The Philadelphia Story (1940)</a></div></div></div><div><button data-testid="dli-add-to-list-button" class="ipc-icon-button ipc-icon-button--base ipc-icon-button--onAccent2" title="Add to list" tabindex="0" aria-label="Add to list" aria-disabled="false"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" class="ipc-icon ipc-icon--add" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" role="presentation"><path d="M18 13h-5v5c0 .55-.45 1-1 1s-1-.45-1-1v-5H6c-.55 0-1-.45-1-1s.45-1 1-1h5V6c0-.55.45-1 1-1s1 .45 1 1v5h5c.55 0 1 .45 1 1s-.45 1-1 1z"></path></svg></button></div></div><div data-testid="dli-bio" class="sc-77f37b3d-2 dpXpaE"><div class="ipc-html-content ipc-html-content--base sc-77f37b3d-3 huKIYr" role="presentation"><div class="ipc-html-content-inner-div" role="presentation">Katharine Houghton Hepburn was born on May 12, 1907 in Hartford, Connecticut to a suffragist, Katharine Martha (Houghton), and a doctor, Thomas Norval Hepburn, who both always encouraged her to speak her mind, develop it fully, and exercise her body to its full potential. An athletic tomboy as a child, she was very close to her brother Tom; at 14 she was devastated to find him dead, the apparent result of accidentally hanging himself while practicing a hanging trick their father had taught them. For many years afterward, she used his November 8 birth date as her own. She became shy around girls her age and was largely schooled at home. She did attend Bryn Mawr College, where she decided to become an actress, appearing in many of their productions.<br/><br/>After graduating, she began getting small roles in plays on Broadway and elsewhere. She always attracted attention, especially for her role in &quot;Art and Mrs. Bottle&quot; (1931). She finally broke into stardom when she took the starring role of the Amazon princess Antiope in &quot;A Warrior&#39;s Husband&quot; (1932). The inevitable film offers followed; after making a few screen tests, she was cast in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0022685/?ls">A Bill of Divorcement (1932)</a>, opposite <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000858/?ls">John Barrymore</a>. The film was a hit, and after agreeing to her salary demands, RKO signed her to a contract. She made five films between 1932 and 1934. For her third, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0024353/?ls">Morning Glory (1933)</a>, she won her first Academy Award. Her fourth, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0024264/?ls">Little Women (1933)</a>, was the most successful picture of its day.<br/><br/>But stories were beginning to leak out, of her haughty behavior off- screen and her refusal to play the Hollywood Game, always wearing slacks and no makeup, never posing for pictures or giving interviews. Audiences were shocked at her unconventional behavior instead of applauding it, and so when she returned to Broadway in 1934 to star in &quot;The Lake&quot;, the critics panned her, and the audiences, who at first bought up tickets, soon deserted her. When she returned to Hollywood, things didn&#39;t get much better. From 1935-1938, she had only two hits: <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0026056/?ls">Alice Adams (1935)</a>, which brought her her second Oscar nomination, and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0029604/?ls">Stage Door (1937)</a>; the many flops included <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0026134/?ls">Break of Hearts (1935)</a>, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0027067/?ls">Sylvia Scarlett (1935)</a>, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0027948/?ls">Mary of Scotland (1936)</a>, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0029454/?ls">Quality Street (1937)</a>, and the now-classic <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0029947/?ls">Baby You Have This (1938)</a>.<br/><br/>With so many flops, she came to be labeled &quot;box-office poison&quot;. She decided to go back to Broadway to star in &quot;The Philadelphia Story&quot; (1938) and was rewarded with a smash. She quickly bought the film rights and so was able to negotiate her way back to Hollywood on her own terms, including her choice of director and co-stars. <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0032904/?ls">The Philadelphia Story (1940)</a> was a box-office hit, and Hepburn, who won her third Oscar nomination for the film, was bankable again. For her next film, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0035567/?ls">Woman of the Year (1942)</a>, she was paired with <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000075/?ls">Spencer Tracy</a>, and the chemistry between them lasted for eight more films, spanning the course of 25 years, and a romance that lasted that long off-screen. (She received her fourth Oscar nomination for the film.) Their films included the very successful <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0041090/?ls">Adam&#39;s Rib (1949)</a>, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0045012/?ls">Pat and Mike (1952)</a>, and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0050307/?ls">Desk Set (1957)</a>.<br/><br/>With <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0043265/?ls">The African Queen (1951)</a>, Hepburn moved into middle-aged spinster roles, receiving her fifth Oscar nomination for the film. She played more of these types of roles throughout the 1950s, and won more Oscar nominations for many of them, including her roles in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0048673/?ls">Summertime (1955)</a>, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0049653/?ls">The Rainmaker (1956)</a>, and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0053318/?ls">Suddenly, Last Summer (1959)</a>. Her film roles became fewer and farther between in the 1960s, as she devoted her time to the ailing Tracy. For one of her film appearances in this decade, in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0056196/?ls">Long Day&#39;s Journey Into Night (1962)</a>, she received her ninth Oscar nomination. After a five-year absence from films, she then made <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0061735/?ls">Guess Who&#39;s Coming to Dinner (1967)</a>, her last film with Tracy and the last film Tracy ever made; he died just weeks after finishing it. It garnered Hepburn her tenth Oscar nomination and her second win. The next year, she did <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0063227/?ls">The Lion in Winter (1968)</a>, which brought her her eleventh Oscar nomination and third win.<br/><br/>In the 1970s, she turned to making made-for-TV films, with <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0070115/?ls">The Glass Menagerie (1973)</a>, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0073310/?ls">Love Among the Ruins (1975)</a>, and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0079000/?ls">The Corn Is Green (1979)</a>. She still continued to make an occasional appearance in feature films, such as <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0073636/?ls">Rooster Cogburn (1975)</a> with <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000078/?ls">John Wayne</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0082846/?ls">On Golden Pond (1981)</a> with <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000020/?ls">Henry Fonda</a>. This last brought her her twelfth Oscar nomination and fourth win - the latter still the record.<br/><br/>She made more TV-films in the 1980s and wrote her autobiography, &#39;Me&#39;, in 1991. Her last feature film was <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0110391/?ls">Love Affair (1994)</a>, with <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000886/?ls">Warren Beatty</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000906/?ls">Annette Bening</a>, and her last TV- film was <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0110732/?ls">One Christmas (1994)</a>. With her health declining, she retired from public life in the mid-1990s. She died at 96 at her home in Old Saybrook, Connecticut.</div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__c"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__tc"><span class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__t" aria-disabled="false"></span><div class="sc-77f37b3d-0 jCbCZO dli-parent"><div class="sc-77f37b3d-1 gJmTWZ"><div class="sc-7c95f518-0 cDAKkN"><div data-testid="nlib-img-container" class="sc-7c95f518-1 iorieb"><div class="ipc-avatar ipc-avatar--base" role="group"><div class="ipc-media ipc-media--avatar ipc-image-media-ratio--avatar ipc-media--circle-radius ipc-media--base ipc-media--custom ipc-avatar__avatar-image ipc-media__img" style="width:60px"><img alt="Daniel Day-Lewis" class="ipc-image" loading="lazy" src="https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjE2NDY2NDc1Ml5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwNjAyMjkwOQ@@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg" srcSet="https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjE2NDY2NDc1Ml5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwNjAyMjkwOQ@@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg 60w, https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjE2NDY2NDc1Ml5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwNjAyMjkwOQ@@._V1_QL75_UX90_CR0,0,90,90_.jpg 90w, https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjE2NDY2NDc1Ml5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwNjAyMjkwOQ@@._V1_QL75_UX120_CR0,0,120,120_.jpg 120w" sizes="50vw, (min-width: 480px) 34vw, (min-width: 600px) 26vw, (min-width: 1024px) 16vw, (min-width: 1280px) 16vw" width="60"/></div><a class="ipc-lockup-overlay ipc-focusable" href="/name/nm0000358/?ref_=ls_i_7" aria-label="Daniel Day-Lewis"><div class="ipc-lockup-overlay__screen"></div></a></div></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-3 krmPLY"><div data-testid="nlib-meter-const-container"></div><div class="ipc-title ipc-title--base ipc-title--title ipc-title-link-no-icon ipc-title--on-textPrimary sc-7c95f518-2 ghWujX" data-testid="nlib-title"><a href="/name/nm0000358/?ref_=ls_t_7" class="ipc-title-link-wrapper" tabindex="0"><h3 class="ipc-title__text">7. Daniel Day-Lewis</h3></a></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-6 iDkHPP"><ul class="ipc-inline-list ipc-inline-list--show-dividers sc-7c95f518-4 lolxqE base" role="presentation" data-testid="nlib-professions"><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Actor</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Writer</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Music Department</li></ul><a class="ipc-link ipc-link--base sc-ab9eb9db-0 iRQWod" tabindex="0" aria-disabled="false" data-testid="nlib-known-for-title" href="/title/tt0469494/?ref_=ls_knf_7">There Will Be Blood (2007)</a></div></div></div><div><button data-testid="dli-add-to-list-button" class="ipc-icon-button ipc-icon-button--base ipc-icon-button--onAccent2" title="Add to list" tabindex="0" aria-label="Add to list" aria-disabled="false"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" class="ipc-icon ipc-icon--add" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" role="presentation"><path d="M18 13h-5v5c0 .55-.45 1-1 1s-1-.45-1-1v-5H6c-.55 0-1-.45-1-1s.45-1 1-1h5V6c0-.55.45-1 1-1s1 .45 1 1v5h5c.55 0 1 .45 1 1s-.45 1-1 1z"></path></svg></button></div></div><div data-testid="dli-bio" class="sc-77f37b3d-2 dpXpaE"><div class="ipc-html-content ipc-html-content--base sc-77f37b3d-3 huKIYr" role="presentation"><div class="ipc-html-content-inner-div" role="presentation">Born in London, England, Daniel Michael Blake Day-Lewis is the second child of <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0086671/?ls">Cecil Day-Lewis</a>, Poet Laureate of the U.K., and his second wife, actress <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0049607/?ls">Jill Balcon</a>. His maternal grandfather was Sir <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0049608/?ls">Michael Balcon</a>, an important figure in the history of British cinema and head of the famous Ealing Studios. His older sister, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0206636/?ls">Tamasin Day-Lewis</a>, is a documentarian. His father was of Northern Irish and English descent, and his mother was Jewish (from a family from Latvia and Poland). Daniel was educated at Sevenoaks School in Kent, which he despised, and the more progressive Bedales in Petersfield, which he adored. He studied acting at the Bristol Old Vic School. Daniel made his film debut in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0067805/?ls">Sunday Bloody Sunday (1971)</a>, but then acted on stage with the Bristol Old Vic and Royal Shakespeare Companies and did not appear on screen again until 1982, when he landed his first adult role, a bit part in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0083987/?ls">Gandhi (1982)</a>. He also appeared on British television that year in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0233760/?ls">Frost in May (1982)</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0084097/?ls">How Many Miles to Babylon? (1982)</a>. Notable theatrical performances include Another Country (1982-83), Dracula (1984) and The Futurists (1986).<br/><br/>His first major supporting role in a feature film was in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0086993/?ls">The Bounty (1984)</a>, quickly followed by <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0091578/?ls">Laundrette (1985)</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0091867/?ls">A Room with a View (1985)</a>. The latter two films opened in New York on the same day, offering audiences and critics evidence of his remarkable range and establishing him as a major talent. The New York Film Critics named him Best Supporting Actor for those performances. In 1986, he appeared on stage in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0264236/?ls">Richard Eyre</a>&#39;s &quot;The Futurists&quot; and on television in Eyre&#39;s production of <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0124758/?ls">The Insurance Man (1986)</a>. He also had a small role in a British/French film, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0091608/?ls">Nanou (1986)</a>. In 1987, he assumed leading-man status in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0442241/?ls">Philip Kaufman</a>&#39;s <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0096332/?ls">The Unbearable Lightness of Being (1988)</a>, followed by a comedic role in the unsuccessful <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0096166/?ls">Stars and Bars (1988)</a>. His brilliant performance as Christy Brown in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0006487/?ls">Jim Sheridan</a>&#39;s <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0097937/?ls">My Left Foot: The Story of Christy Brown (1989)</a> won him numerous awards, including the Academy Award for Best Actor.<br/><br/>He returned to the stage to work again with Eyre, as Hamlet at the National Theater, but was forced to leave the production close to the end of its run because of exhaustion, and has not appeared on stage since. He took a hiatus from film as well until 1992, when he starred in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0104691/?ls">The Last of the Mohicans (1992)</a>, a film that met with mixed reviews but was a great success at the box office. He worked with American director <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000217/?ls">Martin Scorsese</a> in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0106226/?ls">The Age of Innocence (1993)</a>, based on Edith Wharton&#39;s novel. Subsequently, he teamed again with <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0006487/?ls">Jim Sheridan</a> to star in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0107207/?ls">In the Name of the Father (1993)</a>, a critically acclaimed performance that earned him another Academy Award nomination. His next project was in the role of John Proctor in father-in-law <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0007186/?ls">Arthur Miller</a>&#39;s play <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0115988/?ls">Crucible (1996)</a>, directed by <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0405336/?ls">Nicholas Hytner</a>. He worked with Scorsese again to star in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0217505/?ls">Gangs of New York (2002)</a>, another critically acclaimed performance that earned him another Academy Award nomination for Best Actor.<br/><br/>Day-Lewis&#39;s wife, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0589182/?ls">Rebecca Miller</a>, offered him the lead role in her film <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0357110/?ls">The Ballad of Jack and Rose (2005)</a>, in which he played a dying man with regrets over how his wife had evolved and over how he had brought up his teenage daughter. During filming, he arranged to live separate from his wife to achieve the &quot;isolation&quot; needed to focus on his own character&#39;s reality. The film received mixed reviews. In 2007, he starred in director <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000759/?ls">Paul Thomas Anderson</a>&#39;s loose adaptation of Upton Sinclair&#39;s novel &quot;Oil!&quot;, titled <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0469494/?ls">There Will Be Blood (2007)</a>. Day-Lewis received the Academy Award for Best Actor, BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Leading Role, Golden Globe Award for Best Actor - Motion Picture Drama, Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Male Actor in a Leading Role, and a variety of film critics&#39; circle awards for the role. In 2009, Day-Lewis starred in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0551128/?ls">Rob Marshall</a>&#39;s musical adaptation <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0875034/?ls">Nine (2009)</a> as film director Guido Contini. He was nominated for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actor - Motion Picture Musical or Comedy and the Satellite Award for Best Actor - Motion Picture Musical or Comedy.</div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__c"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__tc"><span class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__t" aria-disabled="false"></span><div class="sc-77f37b3d-0 jCbCZO dli-parent"><div class="sc-77f37b3d-1 gJmTWZ"><div class="sc-7c95f518-0 cDAKkN"><div data-testid="nlib-img-container" class="sc-7c95f518-1 iorieb"><div class="ipc-avatar ipc-avatar--base" role="group"><div class="ipc-media ipc-media--avatar ipc-image-media-ratio--avatar ipc-media--circle-radius ipc-media--base ipc-media--custom ipc-avatar__avatar-image ipc-media__img" style="width:60px"><img alt="Sidney Poitier" class="ipc-image" loading="lazy" src="https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTQ0OTE3MzQ2Nl5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwMDc2MDc1NA@@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg" srcSet="https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTQ0OTE3MzQ2Nl5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwMDc2MDc1NA@@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg 60w, https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTQ0OTE3MzQ2Nl5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwMDc2MDc1NA@@._V1_QL75_UX90_CR0,0,90,90_.jpg 90w, https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTQ0OTE3MzQ2Nl5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwMDc2MDc1NA@@._V1_QL75_UX120_CR0,0,120,120_.jpg 120w" sizes="50vw, (min-width: 480px) 34vw, (min-width: 600px) 26vw, (min-width: 1024px) 16vw, (min-width: 1280px) 16vw" width="60"/></div><a class="ipc-lockup-overlay ipc-focusable" href="/name/nm0001627/?ref_=ls_i_8" aria-label="Sidney Poitier"><div class="ipc-lockup-overlay__screen"></div></a></div></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-3 krmPLY"><div data-testid="nlib-meter-const-container"></div><div class="ipc-title ipc-title--base ipc-title--title ipc-title-link-no-icon ipc-title--on-textPrimary sc-7c95f518-2 ghWujX" data-testid="nlib-title"><a href="/name/nm0001627/?ref_=ls_t_8" class="ipc-title-link-wrapper" tabindex="0"><h3 class="ipc-title__text">8. Sidney Poitier</h3></a></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-6 iDkHPP"><ul class="ipc-inline-list ipc-inline-list--show-dividers sc-7c95f518-4 lolxqE base" role="presentation" data-testid="nlib-professions"><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Actor</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Director</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Producer</li></ul><a class="ipc-link ipc-link--base sc-ab9eb9db-0 iRQWod" tabindex="0" aria-disabled="false" data-testid="nlib-known-for-title" href="/title/tt0061811/?ref_=ls_knf_8">In the Heat of the Night (1967)</a></div></div></div><div><button data-testid="dli-add-to-list-button" class="ipc-icon-button ipc-icon-button--base ipc-icon-button--onAccent2" title="Add to list" tabindex="0" aria-label="Add to list" aria-disabled="false"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" class="ipc-icon ipc-icon--add" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" role="presentation"><path d="M18 13h-5v5c0 .55-.45 1-1 1s-1-.45-1-1v-5H6c-.55 0-1-.45-1-1s.45-1 1-1h5V6c0-.55.45-1 1-1s1 .45 1 1v5h5c.55 0 1 .45 1 1s-.45 1-1 1z"></path></svg></button></div></div><div data-testid="dli-bio" class="sc-77f37b3d-2 dpXpaE"><div class="ipc-html-content ipc-html-content--base sc-77f37b3d-3 huKIYr" role="presentation"><div class="ipc-html-content-inner-div" role="presentation">Sidney Poitier was a native of Cat Island, Bahamas, although born, two months prematurely, in Miami during a visit by his parents, Evelyn (Outten) and Reginald James Poitier. He grew up in poverty as the son of farmers, with his father also driving a cab in Nassau. Sidney had little formal education and at the age of 15 was sent to Miami to live with his brother, in order to forestall a growing tendency toward delinquency. In the U.S., he experienced the racial chasm that divides the country, a great shock to a boy coming from a society with a majority of African descent.<br/><br/>At 18, he went to New York, did menial jobs and slept in a bus terminal toilet. A brief stint in the Army as a worker at a veterans&#39; hospital was followed by more menial jobs in Harlem. An impulsive audition at the American Negro Theatre was rejected so forcefully that Poitier dedicated the next six months to overcoming his accent and improving his performing skills. On his second try, he was accepted. Spotted in rehearsal by a casting agent, he won a bit part in the Broadway production of &quot;Lysistrata&quot;, for which he earned good reviews. By the end of 1949, he was having to choose between leading roles on stage and an offer to work for <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0953123/?ls">Darryl F. Zanuck</a> in the film <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0042792/?ls">No Way Out (1950)</a>. His performance as a doctor treating a white bigot got him plenty of notice and led to more roles. Nevertheless, the roles were still less interesting and prominent than those white actors routinely obtained. But seven years later, after turning down several projects he considered demeaning, Poitier got a number of roles that catapulted him into a category rarely if ever achieved by an African-American man of that time, that of leading man. One of these films, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0051525/?ls">The Defiant Ones (1958)</a>, earned Poitier his first Academy Award nomination as Best Actor. Five years later, he won the Oscar for <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0057251/?ls">Lilies of the Field (1963)</a>, the first African American to win for a leading role.<br/><br/>He remained active on stage and screen as well as in the burgeoning Civil Rights movement. His roles in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0061735/?ls">Guess Who&#39;s Coming to Dinner (1967)</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0062376/?ls">To Sir, with Love (1967)</a> were landmarks in helping to break down some social barriers between blacks and whites. Poitier&#39;s talent, conscience, integrity, and inherent likability placed him on equal footing with the white stars of the day. He took on directing and producing chores in the 1970s, achieving success in both arenas.</div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__c"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__tc"><span class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__t" aria-disabled="false"></span><div class="sc-77f37b3d-0 jCbCZO dli-parent"><div class="sc-77f37b3d-1 gJmTWZ"><div class="sc-7c95f518-0 cDAKkN"><div data-testid="nlib-img-container" class="sc-7c95f518-1 iorieb"><div class="ipc-avatar ipc-avatar--base" ipc-title-link-no-icon ipc-title--on-textPrimary sc-7c95f518-2 ghWujX" data-testid="nlib-title"><a href="/name/nm0000007/?ref_=ls_t_9" class="ipc-title-link-wrapper" tabindex="0"><h3 class="ipc-title__text">9. Humphrey Bogart</h3></a></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-6 iDkHPP"><ul class="ipc-inline-list ipc-inline-list--show-dividers sc-7c95f518-4 lolxqE base" role="presentation" data-testid="nlib-professions"><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Actor</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Producer</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Additional Crew</li></ul><a class="ipc-link ipc-link--base sc-ab9eb9db-0 iRQWod" tabindex="0" aria-disabled="false" data-testid="nlib-known-for-title" href="/title/tt0034583/?ref_=ls_knf_9">Casablanca (1942)</a></div></div></div><div><button data-testid="dli-add-to-list-button" class="ipc-icon-button ipc-icon-button--base ipc-icon-button--onAccent2" title="Add to list" tabindex="0" aria-label="Add to list" aria-disabled="false"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" class="ipc-icon ipc-icon--add" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" role="presentation"><path d="M18 13h-5v5c0 .55-.45 1-1 1s-1-.45-1-1v-5H6c-.55 0-1-.45-1-1s.45-1 1-1h5V6c0-.55.45-1 1-1s1 .45 1 1v5h5c.55 0 1 .45 1 1s-.45 1-1 1z"></path></svg></button></div></div><div data-testid="dli-bio" class="sc-77f37b3d-2 dpXpaE"><div class="ipc-html-content ipc-html-content--base sc-77f37b3d-3 huKIYr" role="presentation"><div class="ipc-html-content-inner-div" role="presentation">Humphrey DeForest Bogart was born in New York City, New York, to Maud Humphrey, a famed magazine illustrator and suffragette, and Belmont DeForest Bogart, a moderately wealthy surgeon (who was secretly
addicted to opium). Bogart
was educated at Trinity School, NYC, and was sent to Phillips Academy
in Andover, Massachusetts, in preparation for medical studies at Yale.
He was expelled from Phillips and joined the U.S. Naval Reserve. From
1920 to 1922, he managed a stage company owned by family friend
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0103755/?ls">William A. Brady</a> (the father of actress
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0103567/?ls">Alice Brady</a>), performing a variety of tasks
at Brady&#39;s film studio in New York. He then began regular stage
performances. <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0941233/?ls">Alexander Woollcott</a>
described his acting in a 1922 play as inadequate. In 1930, he gained a
contract with Fox, his feature film debut in a ten-minute short,
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0020714/?ls">Broadway&#39;s Like That (1930)</a>,
co-starring <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0262190/?ls">Ruth Etting</a> and
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000951/?ls">Joan Blondell</a>. Fox released him after two
years. After five years of stage and minor film roles, he had his
breakthrough role in
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0028096/?ls">The Petrified Forest (1936)</a>
from Warner Bros. He won the part over
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000064/?ls">Edward G. Robinson</a> only after the
star, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0001366/?ls">Leslie Howard</a>, threatened
Warner Bros. that he would quit unless Bogart was given the key role of
Duke Mantee, which he had played in the Broadway production with
Howard. The film was a major success and led to a long-term contract
with Warner Bros. From 1936 to 1940, Bogart appeared in 28 films,
usually as a gangster, twice in Westerns and even a horror film. His
landmark year was 1941 (often capitalizing on parts
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0706368/?ls">George Raft</a> had stupidly rejected) with
roles in classics such as
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0033717/?ls">High Sierra (1941)</a> and as Sam Spade
in one of his most fondly remembered films,
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0033870/?ls">The Maltese Falcon (1941)</a>.
These were followed by
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0034583/?ls">Casablanca (1942)</a>,
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0038355/?ls">The Big Sleep (1946)</a>, and
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0040506/?ls">Key Largo (1948)</a>. Bogart, despite his
erratic education, was incredibly well-read and he favored writers and
intellectuals within his small circle of friends. In 1947, he joined
wife <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000002/?ls">Lauren Bacall</a> and other actors
protesting the House Un-American Activities Committee witch hunts. He
also formed his own production company, and the next year made
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0040897/?ls">The Treasure of the Sierra Madre (1948)</a>.
Bogie won the best actor Academy Award for
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0043265/?ls">The African Queen (1951)</a> and
was nominated for <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0034583/?ls">Casablanca (1942)</a>
and as Captain Queeg in
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0046816/?ls">Mutiny of Caine (1954)</a>, a
film made when he was already seriously ill. He died in his sleep at
his Hollywood home following surgeries and a battle with throat cancer.</div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__c"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__tc"><span class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__t" aria-disabled="false"></span><div class="sc-77f37b3d-0 jCbCZO dli-parent"><div class="sc-77f37b3d-1 gJmTWZ"><div class="sc-7c95f518-0 cDAKkN"><div data-testid="nlib-img-container" class="sc-7c95f518-1 iorieb"><div class="ipc-avatar ipc-avatar--base" role="group"><div class="ipc-media ipc-media--avatar ipc-image-media-ratio--avatar ipc-media--circle-radius ipc-media--base ipc-media--custom ipc-avatar__avatar-image ipc-media__img" style="width:60px"><img alt="Clark Gable, c. 1934. MGM / **I.V." class="ipc-image" loading="lazy" src="https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjE1NDY5MjM5Ml5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTYwNTU1OTQ2._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg" srcSet="https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjE1NDY5MjM5Ml5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTYwNTU1OTQ2._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg 60w, https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjE1NDY5MjM5Ml5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTYwNTU1OTQ2._V1_QL75_UX90_CR0,0,90,90_.jpg 90w, https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjE1NDY5MjM5Ml5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTYwNTU1OTQ2._V1_QL75_UX120_CR0,0,120,120_.jpg 120w" sizes="50vw, (min-width: 480px) 34vw, (min-width: 600px) 26vw, (min-width: 1024px) 16vw, (min-width: 1280px) 16vw" width="60"/></div><a class="ipc-lockup-overlay ipc-focusable" href="/name/nm0000022/?ref_=ls_i_10" aria-label="Clark Gable"><div class="ipc-lockup-overlay__screen"></div></a></div></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-3 krmPLY"><div data-testid="nlib-meter-const-container"></div><div class="ipc-title ipc-title--base ipc-title--title ipc-title-link-no-icon ipc-title--on-textPrimary sc-7c95f518-2 ghWujX" data-testid="nlib-title"><a href="/name/nm0000022/?ref_=ls_t_10" class="ipc-title-link-wrapper" tabindex="0"><h3 class="ipc-title__text">10. Clark Gable</h3></a></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-6 iDkHPP"><ul class="ipc-inline-list ipc-inline-list--show-dividers sc-7c95f518-4 lolxqE base" role="presentation" data-testid="nlib-professions"><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Actor</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Producer</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Soundtrack</li></ul><a class="ipc-link ipc-link--base sc-ab9eb9db-0 iRQWod" tabindex="0" aria-disabled="false" data-testid="nlib-known-for-title" href="/title/tt0025316/?ref_=ls_knf_10">It Happened One Night (1934)</a></div></div></div><div><button data-testid="dli-add-to-list-button" class="ipc-icon-button ipc-icon-button--base ipc-icon-button--onAccent2" title="Add to list" tabindex="0" aria-label="Add to list" aria-disabled="false"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" class="ipc-icon ipc-icon--add" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" role="presentation"><path d="M18 13h-5v5c0 .55-.45 1-1 1s-1-.45-1-1v-5H6c-.55 0-1-.45-1-1s.45-1 1-1h5V6c0-.55.45-1 1-1s1 .45 1 1v5h5c.55 0 1 .45 1 1s-.45 1-1 1z"></path></svg></button></div></div><div data-testid="dli-bio" class="sc-77f37b3d-2 dpXpaE"><div class="ipc-html-content ipc-html-content--base sc-77f37b3d-3 huKIYr" role="presentation"><div class="ipc-html-content-inner-div" role="presentation">William Clark Gable was born on February 1, 1901 in Cadiz, Ohio, to Adeline (Hershelman) and William Henry Gable, an oil-well driller. He was of German, Irish, and Swiss-German descent. When he was seven months old, his mother died, and his father sent him to live with his maternal aunt and uncle in Pennsylvania, where he stayed until he was two. His father then returned to take him back to Cadiz. At 16, he quit high school, went to work in an Akron, Ohio, tire factory, and decided
to become an actor after seeing the play &quot;The Bird of Paradise.&quot; He
toured in stock companies, worked oil fields and sold ties. On December 13, 1924, he married <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0227023/?ls">Josephine Dillon</a>, his acting coach and 15 years his senior. Around that time, they moved to Hollywood, so that Clark could concentrate on his acting career. In April 1930, they divorced and a year later, he married Maria Langham (a.k.a. <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm1178752/?ls">Maria Franklin Gable</a>), also about 17 years older than him.<br/><br/>While Gable acted on stage, he became a lifelong friend of <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000859/?ls">Lionel Barrymore</a>. After several failed screen
tests (for Barrymore and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0953123/?ls">Darryl F. Zanuck</a>), Gable was signed in 1930 by MGM&#39;s
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0856921/?ls">Irving Thalberg</a>. He had a small part in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0022243/?ls">The Painted Desert (1931)</a> which starred <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0101955/?ls">William Boyd</a>. <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0001076/?ls">Joan Crawford</a> asked for him as co-star in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0021778/?ls">Dance, Fools, Dance (1931)</a> and the public
loved him manhandling <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0790454/?ls">Norma Shearer</a> in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0021885/?ls">A Free Soul (1931)</a> the same year. His unshaven
lovemaking with bra-less <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0001318/?ls">Jean Harlow</a> in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0023382/?ls">Red Dust (1932)</a> made him MGM&#39;s most
important star.<br/><br/>His acting career then flourished. At one point, he refused an assignment, and the studio
punished him by loaning him out to (at the time) low-rent Columbia
Pictures, which put him in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0001008/?ls">Frank Capra</a>&#39;s <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0025316/?ls">It Happened One Night (1934)</a>, which won him an Academy Award for his performance. The next year saw a starring role in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0026164/?ls">The Call of the Wild (1935)</a> with <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0949835/?ls">Loretta Young</a>, with whom he had an affair (resulting in the birth of a daughter, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0507395/?ls">Judy Lewis</a>).
He returned to far more substantial roles at MGM, such as Fletcher
Christian in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0026752/?ls">Mutiny on the Bounty (1935)</a> and Rhett Butler in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0031381/?ls">Gone with the Wind (1939)</a>.<br/><br/>After divorcing Maria Langham, in March 1939 Clark married <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0001479/?ls">Carole Lombard</a>, but tragedy struck in January 1942 when the plane in which Carole and her mother were flying crashed into Table Rock Mountain, Nevada, killing them both. A grief-stricken Gable joined the US Army Air Force and was off the screen for three years, flying combat missions in Europe. When he returned the studio regarded his salary as excessive and did not renew
his contract. He freelanced, but his films didn&#39;t do well at the box
office. He married Sylvia Ashley, the widow of <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0001196/?ls">Douglas Fairbanks</a>, in 1949. Unfortunately this marriage was short-lived and they divorced in 1952. In July 1955 he married a former sweetheart, Kathleen Williams Spreckles (a.k.a. <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0931035/?ls">Kay Williams</a>) and became stepfather to her two children, Joan and Adolph (&quot;Bunker&quot;) Spreckels III.<br/><br/>On November 16, 1959, Gable became a grandfather when <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0507395/?ls">Judy Lewis</a>, his daughter with <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0949835/?ls">Loretta Young</a>, gave birth to a daughter, Maria. In 1960, Gable&#39;s wife Kay discovered that she was expecting their first child. In early November 1960, he had just completed filming <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0055184/?ls">The Misfits (1961)</a>, when he suffered a heart attack, and died later that month, on November 16, 1960. Gable was buried shortly afterwards in the shrine that he had built for <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0001479/?ls">Carole Lombard</a> and her mother when they died, at Forest Lawn
Cemetery.<br/><br/>In March 1961, Kay Gable gave birth to a boy, whom she named John Clark Gable after his father.</div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__c"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__tc"><span class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__t" aria-disabled="false"></span><div class="sc-77f37b3d-0 jCbCZO dli-parent"><div class="sc-77f37b3d-1 gJmTWZ"><div class="sc-7c95f518-0 cDAKkN"><div data-testid="nlib-img-container" class="sc-7c95f518-1 iorieb"><div class="ipc-avatar ipc-avatar--base" role="group"><div class="ipc-media ipc-media--avatar ipc-image-media-ratio--avatar ipc-media--circle-radius ipc-media--base ipc-media--custom srcSet="https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjQyMTYxODQzMF5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTgwMDA1MTI2NDM@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg 60w, https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjQyMTYxODQzMF5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTgwMDA1MTI2NDM@._V1_QL75_UX90_CR0,0,90,90_.jpg 90w, https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjQyMTYxODQzMF5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTgwMDA1MTI2NDM@._V1_QL75_UX120_CR0,0,120,120_.jpg 120w" sizes="50vw, (min-width: 480px) 34vw, (min-width: 600px) 26vw, (min-width: 1024px) 16vw, (min-width: 1280px) 16vw" width="60"/></div><a class="ipc-lockup-overlay ipc-focusable" href="/name/nm0000006/?ref_=ls_i_11" aria-label="Ingrid Bergman"><div class="ipc-lockup-overlay__screen"></div></a></div></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-3 krmPLY"><div data-testid="nlib-meter-const-container"></div><div class="ipc-title ipc-title--base ipc-title--title ipc-title-link-no-icon ipc-title--on-textPrimary sc-7c95f518-2 ghWujX" data-testid="nlib-title"><a href="/name/nm0000006/?ref_=ls_t_11" class="ipc-title-link-wrapper" tabindex="0"><h3 class="ipc-title__text">11. Ingrid Bergman</h3></a></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-6 iDkHPP"><ul class="ipc-inline-list ipc-inline-list--show-dividers sc-7c95f518-4 lolxqE base" role="presentation" data-testid="nlib-professions"><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Actress</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Producer</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Soundtrack</li></ul><a class="ipc-link ipc-link--base sc-ab9eb9db-0 iRQWod" tabindex="0" aria-disabled="false" data-testid="nlib-known-for-title" href="/title/tt0034583/?ref_=ls_knf_11">Casablanca (1942)</a></div></div></div><div><button data-testid="dli-add-to-list-button" class="ipc-icon-button ipc-icon-button--base ipc-icon-button--onAccent2" title="Add to list" tabindex="0" aria-label="Add to list" aria-disabled="false"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" class="ipc-icon ipc-icon--add" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" role="presentation"><path d="M18 13h-5v5c0 .55-.45 1-1 1s-1-.45-1-1v-5H6c-.55 0-1-.45-1-1s.45-1 1-1h5V6c0-.55.45-1 1-1s1 .45 1 1v5h5c.55 0 1 .45 1 1s-.45 1-1 1z"></path></svg></button></div></div><div data-testid="dli-bio" class="sc-77f37b3d-2 dpXpaE"><div class="ipc-html-content ipc-html-content--base sc-77f37b3d-3 huKIYr" role="presentation"><div class="ipc-html-content-inner-div" role="presentation">Ingrid Bergman was one of the greatest actresses from Hollywood&#39;s lamented Golden Era. Her natural and unpretentious beauty and her immense acting talent made her one of the most celebrated figures in the history of American cinema. Bergman is also one of the most Oscar-awarded actresses, tied with <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000658/?ls">Meryl Streep</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000531/?ls">Frances McDormand</a>, all three of them second only to <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000031/?ls">Katharine Hepburn</a>.<br/><br/>Ingrid Bergman was born on August 29, 1915 in Stockholm, Sweden, to a German mother, Frieda Henrietta (Adler), and a Swedish father, Justus Samuel Bergman, an artist and photographer. Her mother died when she was only two and her father died when she was 12. She went to live with an elderly uncle.<br/><br/>The woman who would be one of the top stars in Hollywood in the 1940s had decided to become an actress after finishing her formal schooling. She had had a taste of acting at age 17 when she played an uncredited role of a girl standing in line in the Swedish film <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0023113/?ls">Landskamp (1932)</a> in 1932 - not much of a beginning for a girl who would be known as &quot;Sweden&#39;s illustrious gift to Hollywood.&quot; Her parents died when she was just a girl and the uncle she lived with didn&#39;t want to stand in the way of Ingrid&#39;s dream. The next year she enrolled at the Royal Dramatic Theatre School in Stockholm but decided that stage acting was not for her. It would be three more years before she would have another chance at a film. When she did, it was more than just a bit part. The film in question was <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0026737/?ls">Munkbrogreven (1935)</a>, where she had a speaking part as Elsa Edlund. After several films that year that established her as a class actress, Ingrid appeared in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0027796/?ls">Intermezzo (1936)</a> as Anita Hoffman. Luckily for her, American producer <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0006388/?ls">David O. Selznick</a> saw it and sent a representative from Selznick International Pictures to gain rights to the story and have Ingrid signed to a contract. Once signed, she came to California and starred in United Artists&#39; 1939 remake of her 1936 film, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0031491/?ls">Intermezzo: A Love Story (1939)</a>, reprising her original role. The film was a hit and so was Ingrid.<br/><br/>Her beauty was unlike anything the movie industry had seen before and her acting was superb. Hollywood was about to find out that they had the most versatile actress the industry had ever seen. Here was a woman who truly cared about the craft she represented. The public fell in love with her. Ingrid was under contract to go back to Sweden to film <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0031270/?ls">En enda natt (1939)</a> in 1939 and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0032655/?ls">June Night (1940)</a> in 1940. Back in the US she appeared in three films, all well-received. She made only one film in 1942, but it was the classic <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0034583/?ls">Casablanca (1942)</a> opposite <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000007/?ls">Humphrey Bogart</a>.<br/><br/>Ingrid was choosing her roles well. In 1943 she was nominated for an Academy Award for her role in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0035896/?ls">For Whom the Bell Tolls (1943)</a>, the only film she made that year. The critics and public didn&#39;t forget her when she made <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0036855/?ls">Gaslight (1944)</a> the following year--her role of Paula Alquist got her the Oscar for Best Actress. In 1945 Ingrid played in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0038109/?ls">Spellbound (1945)</a>, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0038053/?ls">Saratoga Trunk (1945)</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0037536/?ls">The Bells of St. Mary&#39;s (1945)</a>, for which she received her third Oscar nomination for her role of Sister Benedict. She made no films in 1947, but bounced back with a fourth nomination for <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0040491/?ls">Joan of Arc (1948)</a>. In 1949 she went to Italy to film <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0041931/?ls">Stromboli (Terra di Dio) (1950)</a>, directed by
<a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0744023/?ls">Roberto Rossellini</a>. She fell in love with him and left her husband, Dr. Peter Lindstrom, and daughter, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0512523/?ls">Pia Lindström</a>. America&#39;s &quot;moral guardians&quot; in the press and the pulpits were outraged. She was pregnant and decided to remain in Italy, where her son was born. In 1952 Ingrid had twins, Isotta and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000618/?ls">Isabella Rossellini</a>, who became an outstanding actress in her own right, as did Pia.<br/><br/>Ingrid continued to make films in Italy and finally returned to Hollywood in 1956 in the title role in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0048947/?ls">Anastasia (1956)</a>, which was filmed in England. For this she won her second Academy Award. She had scarcely missed a beat. Ingrid continued to bounce between Europe and the US making movies, and fine ones at that. A film with Ingrid Bergman was sure to be a quality production. In her final big-screen performance in 1978&#39;s <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0077711/?ls">Autumn Sonata (1978)</a> she had her final Academy Award nomination. Though she didn&#39;t win, many felt it was the most sterling performance of her career. Ingrid retired, but not before she gave an outstanding performance in the mini-series <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0084914/?ls">A Woman Called Golda (1982)</a>, a film about Israeli prime minister <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0576954/?ls">Golda Meir</a>. For this she won an Emmy Award as Best Actress, but, unfortunately, she did not live to see the fruits of her labor.<br/><br/>Ingrid died from cancer on August 29, 1982, her 67th birthday, in London, England.</div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__c"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__tc"><span class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__t" aria-disabled="false"></span><div class="sc-77f37b3d-0 jCbCZO dli-parent"><div class="sc-77f37b3d-1 gJmTWZ"><div class="sc-7c95f518-0 cDAKkN"><div data-testid="nlib-img-container" class="sc-7c95f518-1 iorieb"><div class="ipc-avatar ipc-avatar--base" role="group"><div class="ipc-media ipc-media--avatar ipc-image-media-ratio--avatar ipc-media--circle-radius ipc-media--base ipc-media--custom ipc-avatar__avatar-image ipc-media__img" style="width:60px"><img alt="Leonardo DiCaprio at an event for Inception (2010)" class="ipc-image" srcSet="https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjI0MTg3MzI0M15BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwMzQyODU2Mw@@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg 60w, https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjI0MTg3MzI0M15BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwMzQyODU2Mw@@._V1_QL75_UX90_CR0,0,90,90_.jpg 90w, https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjI0MTg3MzI0M15BMl5BanBnXkFtZTcwMzQyODU2Mw@@._V1_QL75_UX120_CR0,0,120,120_.jpg 120w" sizes="50vw, (min-width: 480px) 34vw, (min-width: 600px) 26vw, (min-width: class="ipc-lockup-overlay__screen"></div></a></div></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-3 krmPLY"><div data-testid="nlib-meter-const-container"></div><div class="ipc-title ipc-title--base ipc-title--title ipc-title-link-no-icon ipc-title--on-textPrimary sc-7c95f518-2 ghWujX" data-testid="nlib-title"><a href="/name/nm0000138/?ref_=ls_t_12" class="ipc-title-link-wrapper" tabindex="0"><h3 class="ipc-title__text">12. Leonardo DiCaprio</h3></a></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-6 iDkHPP"><ul class="ipc-inline-list ipc-inline-list--show-dividers sc-7c95f518-4 lolxqE base" role="presentation" data-testid="nlib-professions"><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Producer</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Actor</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Writer</li></ul><a class="ipc-link ipc-link--base sc-ab9eb9db-0 iRQWod" tabindex="0" aria-disabled="false" data-testid="nlib-known-for-title" href="/title/tt1375666/?ref_=ls_knf_12">Inception (2010)</a></div></div></div><div><button data-testid="dli-add-to-list-button" class="ipc-icon-button ipc-icon-button--base ipc-icon-button--onAccent2" title="Add to list" tabindex="0" aria-label="Add to list" aria-disabled="false"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" class="ipc-icon ipc-icon--add" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" role="presentation"><path d="M18 13h-5v5c0 .55-.45 1-1 1s-1-.45-1-1v-5H6c-.55 0-1-.45-1-1s.45-1 1-1h5V6c0-.55.45-1 1-1s1 .45 1 1v5h5c.55 0 1 .45 1 1s-.45 1-1 1z"></path></svg></button></div></div><div data-testid="dli-bio" class="sc-77f37b3d-2 dpXpaE"><div class="ipc-html-content ipc-html-content--base sc-77f37b3d-3 huKIYr" role="presentation"><div class="ipc-html-content-inner-div" role="presentation">Few actors in the world have had a career quite as diverse as Leonardo DiCaprio&#39;s. DiCaprio has gone from relatively humble beginnings, as a supporting cast member of the sitcom <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0088527/?ls">Growing Pains (1985)</a> and low budget horror movies, such as <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0101627/?ls">Critters 3 (1991)</a>, to a major teenage heartthrob in the 1990s, as the hunky lead actor in movies such as <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0117509/?ls">Romeo + Juliet (1996)</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0120338/?ls">Titanic (1997)</a>, to then become a leading man in Hollywood blockbusters, made by internationally renowned directors such as <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000217/?ls">Martin Scorsese</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0634240/?ls">Christopher Nolan</a>.<br/><br/>Leonardo Wilhelm DiCaprio was born in Los Angeles, California, the only child of <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm2638069/?ls">Irmelin DiCaprio</a> (née Indenbirken) and former comic book artist <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm1096247/?ls">George DiCaprio</a>. His father is of Italian and German descent, and his mother, who is German-born, is of German, Ukrainian and Russian ancestry. His middle name, &quot;Wilhelm&quot;, was his maternal grandfather&#39;s first name. Leonardo&#39;s father had achieved minor status as an artist and distributor of cult comic book titles, and was even depicted in several issues of American Splendor, the cult semi-autobiographical comic book series by the late &#39;Harvey Pekar&#39;, a friend of George&#39;s. Leonardo&#39;s performance skills became obvious to his parents early on, and after signing him up with a talent agent who wanted Leonardo to perform under the stage name &quot;Lenny Williams&quot;, DiCaprio began appearing on a number of television commercials and educational programs.<br/><br/>DiCaprio began attracting the attention of producers, who cast him in small roles in a number of television series, such as <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0094540/?ls">Roseanne (1988)</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0096661/?ls">The New Lassie (1989)</a>, but it wasn&#39;t until 1991 that DiCaprio made his film debut in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0101627/?ls">Critters 3 (1991)</a>, a low-budget horror movie. While <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0101627/?ls">Critters 3 (1991)</a> did little to help showcase DiCaprio&#39;s acting abilities, it did help him develop his show-reel, and attract the attention of the people behind the hit sitcom <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0088527/?ls">Growing Pains (1985)</a>, in which Leonardo was cast in the &quot;Cousin Oliver&quot; role of a young homeless boy who moves in with the Seavers. While DiCaprio&#39;s stint on <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0088527/?ls">Growing Pains (1985)</a> was very short, as the sitcom was axed the year after he joined, it helped bring DiCaprio into the public&#39;s attention and, after the sitcom ended, DiCaprio began auditioning for roles in which he would get the chance to prove his acting chops.<br/><br/>Leonardo took up a diverse range of roles in the early 1990s, including a mentally challenged youth in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0108550/?ls">What&#39;s Eating Gilbert Grape (1993)</a>, a young gunslinger in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0114214/?ls">The Quick and the Dead (1995)</a> and a drug addict in one of his most challenging roles to date, Jim Carroll in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0112461/?ls">The Basketball Diaries (1995)</a>, a role which the late <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000203/?ls">River Phoenix</a> originally expressed interest in. While these diverse roles helped establish Leonardo&#39;s reputation as an actor, it wasn&#39;t until his role as Romeo Montague in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0525303/?ls">Baz Luhrmann</a>&#39;s <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0117509/?ls">Romeo + Juliet (1996)</a> that Leonardo became a household name, a true movie star. The following year, DiCaprio starred in another movie about doomed lovers, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0120338/?ls">Titanic (1997)</a>, which went on to beat all box office records held before then, as, at the time, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0120338/?ls">Titanic (1997)</a> became the highest grossing movie of all time, and cemented DiCaprio&#39;s reputation as a teen heartthrob. Following his work on <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0120338/?ls">Titanic (1997)</a>, DiCaprio kept a low profile for a number of years, with roles in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0120744/?ls">The Man in the Iron Mask (1998)</a> and the low-budget <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0163978/?ls">The Beach (2000)</a> being some of his few notable roles during this period.<br/><br/>In 2002, he burst back into screens throughout the world with leading roles in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0264464/?ls">Catch Me If You Can (2002)</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0217505/?ls">Gangs of New York (2002)</a>, his first of many collaborations with director <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000217/?ls">Martin Scorsese</a>. With a current salary of $20 million a movie, DiCaprio is now one of the biggest movie stars in the world. However, he has not limited his professional career to just acting in movies, as DiCaprio is a committed environmentalist, who is actively involved in many environmental causes, and his commitment to this issue led to his involvement in The 11th Hour, a documentary movie about the state of the natural environment. As someone who has gone from small roles in television commercials to one of the most respected actors in the world, DiCaprio has had one of the most diverse careers in cinema. DiCaprio continued to defy conventions about the types of roles he would accept, and with his career now seeing him leading all-star casts in action thrillers such as <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0407887/?ls">The Departed (2006)</a>, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt1130884/?ls">Shutter Island (2010)</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0634240/?ls">Christopher Nolan</a>&#39;s <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt1375666/?ls">Inception (2010)</a>, DiCaprio continues to wow audiences by refusing to conform to any cliché about actors.<br/><br/>In 2012, he played a mustache twirling villain in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt1853728/?ls">Django Unchained (2012)</a>, and then tragic literary character Jay Gatsby in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt1343092/?ls">The Great Gatsby (2013)</a> and Jordan Belfort in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0993846/?ls">The Wolf of Wall Street (2013)</a>.<br/><br/>DiCaprio is passionate about environmental and humanitarian causes, having donated $1,000,000 to earthquake relief efforts in 2010, the same year he contributed $1,000,000 to the Wildlife Conservation Society.</div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__c"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__tc"><span class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__t" aria-disabled="false"></span><div class="sc-77f37b3d-0 jCbCZO dli-parent"><div class="sc-77f37b3d-1 gJmTWZ"><div class="sc-7c95f518-0 cDAKkN"><div data-testid="nlib-img-container" class="sc-7c95f518-1 iorieb"><div class="ipc-avatar ipc-avatar--base" role="group"><div class="ipc-media ipc-media--avatar ipc-image-media-ratio--avatar ipc-media--circle-radius ipc-media--base ipc-media--custom class="ipc-lockup-overlay__screen"></div></a></div></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-3 krmPLY"><div data-testid="nlib-meter-const-container"></div><div class="ipc-title ipc-title--base ipc-title--title ipc-title-link-no-icon ipc-title--on-textPrimary sc-7c95f518-2 ghWujX" data-testid="nlib-title"><a href="/name/nm0000056/?ref_=ls_t_13" class="ipc-title-link-wrapper" tabindex="0"><h3 class="ipc-title__text">13. Paul Newman</h3></a></div><div class="sc-7c95f518-6 iDkHPP"><ul class="ipc-inline-list ipc-inline-list--show-dividers sc-7c95f518-4 lolxqE base" role="presentation" data-testid="nlib-professions"><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Actor</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Producer</li><li role="presentation" class="ipc-inline-list__item sc-7c95f518-5 eXHlql">Director</li></ul><a class="ipc-link ipc-link--base sc-ab9eb9db-0 iRQWod" tabindex="0" aria-disabled="false" data-testid="nlib-known-for-title" href="/title/tt0054997/?ref_=ls_knf_13">The Hustler (1961)</a></div></div></div><div><button data-testid="dli-add-to-list-button" class="ipc-icon-button ipc-icon-button--base ipc-icon-button--onAccent2" title="Add to list" tabindex="0" aria-label="Add to list" aria-disabled="false"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" class="ipc-icon ipc-icon--add" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor" role="presentation"><path d="M18 13h-5v5c0 .55-.45 1-1 1s-1-.45-1-1v-5H6c-.55 0-1-.45-1-1s.45-1 1-1h5V6c0-.55.45-1 1-1s1 .45 1 1v5h5c.55 0 1 .45 1 1s-.45 1-1 1z"></path></svg></button></div></div><div data-testid="dli-bio" class="sc-77f37b3d-2 dpXpaE"><div class="ipc-html-content ipc-html-content--base sc-77f37b3d-3 huKIYr" role="presentation"><div class="ipc-html-content-inner-div" role="presentation">Screen legend, superstar, and the man with the most famous blue eyes in movie history, Paul Leonard Newman was born on January 26, 1925, in Cleveland, Ohio, the second son of Arthur Sigmund Newman (died 1950) and Theresa Fetsko (died 1982). His elder brother was <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0627983/?ls">Arthur S. Newman Jr.</a>, named for their father, a Jewish businessman who owned a successful sporting goods store and was the son of emigrants from Poland and Hungary. Newman&#39;s mother (born Terézia Fecková, daughter of Stefan Fecko and Mária Polenak) was a Roman Catholic Slovak from Homonna, Pticie (former Austro-Hungarian Empire), who became a practicing Christian Scientist. She and her brother, Newman&#39;s uncle Joe, had an interest in the creative arts, and it rubbed off on him. He acted in grade school and high school plays. The Newmans were well-to-do and Paul Newman grew up in affluent Shaker Heights. Before he became an actor, Newman ran the family sporting goods store in Cleveland, Ohio.<br/><br/>By 1950, the 25-year-old Newman had been kicked out of Ohio University, where he belonged to the Phi Kappa Tau fraternity, for unruly behavior (denting the college president&#39;s car with a beer keg), served three years in the United States Navy during World War II as a radio operator, graduated from Ohio&#39;s Kenyon College, married his first wife, Jacqueline &quot;Jackie&quot; Witte (born 1929), and had his first child, Scott. That same year, his father died. When he became successful in later years, Newman said if he had any regrets it would be that his father was not around to witness his success. He brought Jackie back to Shaker Heights and he ran his father&#39;s store for a short period. Then, knowing that wasn&#39;t the career path he wanted to take, he moved Jackie and Scott to New Haven, Connecticut, where he attended Yale University&#39;s School of Drama.<br/><br/>While doing a play there, Newman was spotted by two agents, who invited him to come to New York City to pursue a career as a professional actor. After moving to New York, he acted in guest spots for various television series and in 1953 came a big break. He got the part of understudy of the lead role in the successful Broadway play &quot;Picnic&quot;. Through this play, he met actress Joanne Woodward (born 1930), who was also an understudy in the play. While they got on very well and there was a strong attraction, Newman was married and his second child, Susan, was born that year. During this time, Newman was accepted into the much admired and popular New York Actors Studio, although he did not actually audition.<br/><br/>In 1954, a film Newman was very reluctant to do was released, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0047494/?ls">The Silver Chalice (1954)</a>. He considered his performance in this costume epic to be so bad that he took out a full-page ad in a trade paper apologizing for it to anyone who might have seen it. He had always been embarrassed about the film and reveled in making fun of it. He immediately wanted to return to the stage, and performed in &quot;The Desperate Hours&quot;. In 1956, he got the chance to redeem himself in the film world by portraying boxer <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0337200/?ls">Rocky Graziano</a> in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0049778/?ls">Somebody Up There Likes Me (1956)</a>, and critics praised his performance. In 1957, with a handful of films to his credit, he was cast in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0051878/?ls">The Long Hot Summer (1958)</a>, co-starring <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0940946/?ls">Joanne Woodward</a>.<br/><br/>During the shooting of this film, they realized they were meant to be together and by now, so did his then-wife Jackie, who gave Newman a divorce. He and Woodward wed in Las Vegas in January 1958. They went on to have three daughters together and raised them in Westport, Connecticut. In 1959, Newman received his first Academy Award nomination for Best Actor, in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0051459/?ls">Cat on a Hot Tin Roof (1958)</a>. The 1960s would bring Newman into superstar status, as he became one of the most popular actors of the decade, and garnered three more Best Actor Oscar nominations, for <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0054997/?ls">The Hustler (1961)</a>, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0057163/?ls">Hud (1963)</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0061512/?ls">Cool Hand Luke (1967)</a>. In 1968, his debut directorial effort <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0063483/?ls">Rachel, Rachel (1968)</a> was given good marks, and although the film and Woodward were nominated for Oscars, Newman was not nominated for Best Director. However, he did win a Golden Globe Award for his direction.<br/><br/>1969 brought the popular screen duo of Newman and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0000602/?ls">Robert Redford</a> together for the first time when <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0064115/?ls">Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid (1969)</a> was released. It was a box office smash. Through the 1970s, Newman had hits and misses from such popular films as <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0070735/?ls">The Sting (1973)</a> and <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0072308/?ls">The Towering Inferno (1974)</a> to lesser known films as <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0068853/?ls">The Life and Times of Judge Roy Bean (1972)</a> to a cult classic <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0076723/?ls">Slap Shot (1977)</a>. After the death of his only son, Scott, in 1978, Newman&#39;s personal life and film choices moved in a different direction. His acting work in the 1980s and on is what is often most praised by critics today. He became more at ease with himself and it was evident in <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0084855/?ls">The Verdict (1982)</a> for which he received his sixth Best Actor Oscar nomination and, in 1987, finally received his first Oscar for <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0090863/?ls">The Color of Money (1986)</a>, almost thirty years after Woodward had won hers. Friend and director of <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/title/tt0049778/?ls">Somebody Up There Likes Me (1956)</a>, <a class="ipc-md-link ipc-md-link--entity" href="/name/nm0936404/?ls">Robert Wise</a> accepted the award on Newman&#39;s behalf as the actor did not attend the ceremony.<br/><br/>Films were not the only thing on his mind during this period. A passionate race car driver since the early 1970s (despite being color-blind), he was co-founder of Newman-Haas racing in 1982, and also founded &quot;Newman&#39;s Own&quot;, a successful line of food products that has earned in excess of $100 million, every penny of which Newman donated to charity. He also started The Hole in the Wall Gang Camps, an organization for children with serious illness. He was as well known for his philanthropic ways and highly successful business ventures as he was for his legendary actor status.<br/><br/>Newman&#39;s marriage to Woodward lasted a half-century. Connecticut was their primary residence after leaving Hollywood and moving East in 1960. Renowned for his sense of humor, in 1998 he quipped that he was a little embarrassed to see his salad dressing grossing more than his movies. During his later years, he still attended races, was much involved in his charitable organizations, and in 2006, he opened a restaurant called Dressing Room, which helps out the Westport Country Playhouse, a place in which Newman took great pride. In 2007, while the public was largely unaware of the serious illness from which he was suffering, Newman made some headlines when he said he was losing his invention and confidence in his acting abilities and that acting was &quot;pretty much a closed book for me&quot;. A smoker for many years, Newman died on September 26, 2008, aged 83, from lung cancer.</div></div></div></div></div></div></li><li class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__c"><div class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__tc"><span class="ipc-metadata-list-summary-item__t" aria-disabled="false"></span><div class="sc-77f37b3d-0 jCbCZO dli-parent"><div class="sc-77f37b3d-1 gJmTWZ"><div class="sc-7c95f518-0 cDAKkN"><div data-testid="nlib-img-container" class="sc-7c95f518-1 iorieb"><div class="ipc-avatar ipc-avatar--base" srcSet="https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTQzMTc5MDg0OF5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTgwODE4NjMzNDE@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg 60w, https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTQzMTc5MDg0OF5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTgwODE4NjMzNDE@._V1_QL75_UX90_CR0,0,90,90_.jpg 90w, https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTQzMTc5MDg0OF5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTgwODE4NjMzNDE@._V1_QL75_UX120_CR0,0,120,120_.jpg 120w" sizes="50vw, (min-width: 480px) 34vw, (min-width: 600px) 26vw, (min-width:
